title: Fed Hawkish-to-Dovish Pivot: Soft Jobs Data Drags Yields Lower and Revives Rate-Cut Hopes
content: The window's defining shift was a swing in the rates outlook. Entering the period, resurgent energy-driven inflation had markets braced for tightening, and the Fed's 29 July hold at 3.50-3.75% drew three dissents favouring a hike, keeping the USD firm and the long end heavy. The narrative then inverted: a startling July payrolls report showed employment falling around 23,000 with roughly 103,000 of prior gains revised away and wage growth slowing to 3.2%, while cooling inflation prints and softer oil eased price fears. Markets rapidly repriced from hike risk towards eventual cuts. UST yields fell across the curve, the 10-year easing towards 4.65% and the 2-year near 4.20%, and the dollar softened from its mid-window highs. The repricing rippled into equities, gold and FX, making every data release pivotal for cross-asset direction.

title: Equities Melt Up to Records as Blockbuster Big-Tech Earnings Reignite the AI Trade
content: Wall Street staged a powerful melt-up to fresh records, led once again by AI-linked megacaps. After mid-July profit-taking and a brief rotation away from big tech, strong second-quarter earnings rekindled the trade: Microsoft leapt around 16% on accelerating Azure growth and Amazon revived confidence in AI infrastructure spending, driving the S&P 500's technology sector to its best session since April 2025. Apple briefly touched a 5tn dollar valuation, overtaking Nvidia as the most valuable company. The rally broadened and accelerated as the dovish rates repricing removed a headwind: the S&P 500 climbed above 7,700 to record closes near 7,758, the Dow cleared 54,000 and the Nasdaq jumped over 5% on a semiconductor bounce-back. The advance underscored persistent index concentration, keeping breadth, positioning and the durability of AI capex central to the equity outlook.
